origin.description: Locate every segment between text boundaries.
origin.usage: stri_locate_all_boundaries(str, omit_no_match = FALSE, get_length = FALSE, ..., opts_brkiter = NULL)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A character vector, or an object coerced to character.

arguments.name: omit_no_match
arguments.text: TRUE returns a matrix with zero rows when there is no segment.

arguments.name: get_length
arguments.text: TRUE makes the second column the length. A miss on a real string is then -1.

arguments.name: opts_brkiter
arguments.text: Break-iterator settings. NULL uses the line breaker.

origin.details: Vectorized over str. A skip_* flag drops every segment whose ending boundary has that ICU rule status. The skipped text is not joined to the next segment. An omitted skip acts as FALSE. Indexes are 1-based inclusive code points. Each list element is an integer matrix with columns start and end, or start and length. A missing string is one NA row. An empty string or a total miss is one NA row, or -1 when get_length is TRUE, unless omit_no_match is TRUE.
origin.example:
loc <- stri_locate_all_boundaries("abc", type = "character")[[1]]
cat(paste0('stri_locate_all_boundaries("abc", type = "character") starts at ', paste(loc[, 1], collapse = ", "), '.\n'))

translation.description: Locate every segment between text boundaries.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A string, NA, or a list of those. None is an empty vector.

arguments.name: omit_no_match
arguments.text: True returns a matrix with zero rows when there is no segment.

arguments.name: get_length
arguments.text: True makes the second column the length. A miss on a real string is then -1.

arguments.name: opts_brkiter
arguments.text: A dict of supplied break-iterator settings.

translation.details: A skip_* flag drops every segment whose ending boundary has that ICU rule status. The skipped text is not joined to the next segment. An omitted skip is false. Positions are 1-based inclusive code points. BreakIterator indexes are UTF-16 code units and are converted before they are returned. NA stays missing. The string "NA" is text. Each list element is a matrix of rows. Columns are start and end, or start and length. A missing string is one NA row. An empty string or a total miss is one NA row, or -1 when get_length is true, unless omit_no_match is true.
translation.value: A list of matrices. Each matrix is a list of [start, end] or [start, length] rows.
translation.example:
from stringi.boundary import stri_locate_all_boundaries
loc = stri_locate_all_boundaries("abc", type="character")[0]
starts = ", ".join(str(row[0]) for row in loc)
print(f'stri_locate_all_boundaries("abc", type="character") starts at {starts}.')
